title: The Last Supper and Pentecost...HERE!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Join Joel in learning how the Upper Room was found and identified, and marvel with him that we can still visit this site where Jesus shared his last supper with his disciples and instructed them to wait for the Day of Pentecost.

title: Jesus' Tomb Explained--the evidence & the story!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Join Joel as he travels from Israel to Rome to Turkey, to explain the evidence for and tell the story of the first and most important archaeological dig ever conducted...the excavation of the Tomb of Jesus.

title: Archaeology of Jacob's Well at Shechem
author: Expedition Bible
description: If there is one place where we can know for certain that Jesus was right there, it is at Jacob's Well. How can we know? In the Gospel of John, chapter 4 provides key details needed to be able to trace the archaeology to anchor that well as the very place where Jesus offered the Samaritan woman "living water."

title: Prophet Found Through Archaeology - Bible Proves True
author: Expedition Bible
description: Join Joel at Tell Deir 'Alla in Jordan's Jordan Valley, where a 1967 excavation uncovered a plastered wall inscription naming "Balaam son of Beor, the seer" — the same prophet from the book of Numbers. Found completely independent of the Bible, this discovery shows the people and events Scripture describes are rooted in real history, not myth.

title: What Kind of Bears Are in the Bible?
author: Expedition Bible
description: Join Joel as he investigates the bears described in Scripture — from the bear David fought off while shepherding to the two bears that mauled boys near Bethel. Using biblical geography, Byzantine-era mosaics, and the history of brown bear distribution, Joel makes the case that these were grizzly bears, once native to Israel's forested highlands until the species' local extinction in the 1800s.

title: The Oldest Yahweh Inscription Ever Found!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to the temple of Soleb in Sudan to see the oldest known inscription naming Yahweh — an Egyptian hieroglyphic text from Pharaoh Amenhotep III reading "Land of the nomads of Yahweh," dating to the late 15th century BC. He connects this archaeological find to the biblical description of the wandering Israelites of that same period as a people identified with their God, Yahweh.

title: The Lost 10 Tribes of Israel...SOLVED!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel examines the Assyrian conquest of the northern kingdom of Israel and asks whether the "lost ten tribes" were truly lost. He traces God's promise in Micah to gather all of Jacob into Jerusalem, archaeological evidence of a massive refugee population on Jerusalem's Western Hill dating to this period, and the biblical and Assyrian records of Sennacherib's siege of Jerusalem — arguing that the remnant of all twelve tribes was preserved within the city rather than lost.

title: Archaeological Evidence for Jesus of Nazareth: The "Jesus is Present"
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel explores an early Christian inscription at Bayt Loya (Khirbet Beit Loya), southwest of Jerusalem near Lachish — a Greek inscription found deep in a cave reading "Jesus is present," bracketed by early cross symbols and dated to the late 2nd or early 3rd century AD. He connects the location — hidden underground during a period of Roman persecution — and the inscription's message to Jesus's promise that where two or three gather in his name, he is present among them, presenting it as rare direct archaeological evidence for the historical Jesus.

title: The Bible Gets It Right: Jesus' Crucifixion Matches History
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel presents archaeological evidence for Roman crucifixion by nailing. He examines the ossuary of Yehohanan, discovered in a Jerusalem tomb in 1968 with an iron nail still embedded through his heel bone, and a second set of nails fused to hand bones found in a nearby tomb in 1970. Together these finds provide a composite picture of first-century crucifixion — nailed through the ankles and hands — matching the New Testament's description of how Jesus was crucified.

title: Jesus, the Grain of Wheat
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel walks through the life cycle of wheat — dormant seed, germination, and abundant harvest — to explain Jesus's analogy for his own death and resurrection. He connects Daniel's prophecy that the Messiah would be "cut off," Jesus's teaching that a grain of wheat must die to produce many seeds, and Pentecost (the biblical wheat harvest) with the moment about 3,000 souls were added to the believers after Peter's sermon.

title: Sulfur Balls of Sodom and Gomorrah
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel visits Bab edh-Dhra and Numeira, two early Bronze Age sites on the southeast shore of the Dead Sea identified with Sodom and Gomorrah, where excavators found extensive fire-destruction layers filled with burned pottery and human remains, with both cities and their cemeteries destroyed simultaneously and never rebuilt. He then tracks down naturally occurring sulfur balls preserved along the Dead Sea shoreline and demonstrates their flammability, connecting this geological evidence to the Bible's description of burning sulfur raining down on Sodom and Gomorrah.

title: Archaeological Evidence for Giants in the Bible?
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel examines a 1962 discovery at Kfar Monash, Israel — a hoard of ancient copper weapons including four massive spearheads and roughly 800 copper armor scales. He compares the largest spearhead to the biblical description of the giant Ishbi-Benob's spear (2 Samuel 21:16) and the pile of armor scales to Goliath's bronze coat of mail (1 Samuel 17:4-5), noting that matching armor scales were also found at Tel Gath, Goliath's hometown, and argues this correlation supports the historicity of biblical giants — while noting that secular archaeologists interpret the same finds as decorative rather than functional.

title: Exploring Babylon and the Prophecies Against Her
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to the ancient site of Babylon in Iraq, using 19th-century German excavation maps to trace the boundaries of the city walls built up under Nebuchadnezzar II. He documents the site today as a vast, uninhabited ruin overrun by wolves, jackals, foxes, and owls, arguing this matches the biblical prophecies that Babylon would become permanently desolate and a haunt for wild animals rather than a re-inhabited city.

title: Jesus, The Soul Shepherd
author: Expedition Bible
description: Filmed among Bedouin shepherds in Israel, Joel uses the daily realities of real shepherding — leading flocks to pasture and water, guarding sheep from wolves, using sheep pens, separating sheep from goats — to unpack the Bible's shepherd metaphor for Jesus and the human soul. He weaves together Psalm 23, Ezekiel's promise that God himself will seek out the lost, and Jesus's own words as the good shepherd and gate for the sheep to explain concepts like sin, salvation, and the presence of God as protection from evil.

title: King David's Tomb: Part 1 -- Finding It
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel traces how archaeologist Raymond Weill used the Bible as a "treasure map" in 1913-14, combining 1 Kings' statement that David was buried in the City of David with Nehemiah's description of the city wall's sections, to pinpoint and excavate a group of monumental rock-cut tombs in Jerusalem — one of which, T1, contains a sarcophagus Weill identified as the probable resting place of King David. Joel then turns to Psalm 16, arguing David's words about a coming one whose body would not decay point beyond David himself to the Messiah's resurrection.

title: King David's Tomb: Part 2 - Which Is The Correct Tomb?
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel contrasts two traditions for King David's tomb — a medieval story placing it on Jerusalem's Western Hill (Mount Zion), first recorded by a 12th-century traveler, versus Raymond Weill's 1913 discovery in the City of David, which the Bible actually supports. He shows how archaeologist Kathleen Kenyon later reinterpreted Weill's tombs as cisterns despite acknowledging they don't match known cistern designs, and highlights Weill's discovery of the first-century BC Theodotus inscription naming a nearby synagogue. Joel argues this synagogue's proximity to David's tomb sets the scene for Peter's Pentecost sermon in Acts, where Peter cites Psalm 16 to argue that David's prophecy of a resurrected, non-decaying body pointed to Jesus, since David's own body remained buried nearby.

title: Jesus, the Pressed Olive
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel explains that ancient lamps burned oil pressed from olives, then draws a metaphor from Gethsemane — whose name means "olive press" — where Jesus prayed under immense agony before his arrest. Just as olives are crushed under pressure to yield light-giving oil, Joel frames Jesus's suffering there as the pressure that produced him becoming, in his sacrifice, "a great light" for a world in darkness.

title: Evidence for Ancient Israel Discovered in Egypt
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Egypt to examine the Merneptah Stele, discovered by Flinders Petrie in 1896 at the mortuary temple of Pharaoh Merneptah in Luxor. Dating to around 1210 BC, the inscription's mention of "Israel" is the earliest known reference to the name outside the Bible, and it depicts Israel without the city-state symbol used for kingdoms — matching the biblical Judges period, when Israel had not yet formed a monarchy.

title: Is the Bible used in Archaeology?
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel visits five active excavations in Israel — Gezer, Jericho, Hazor, Gath, and Jerusalem's Upper City — asking each dig director whether they use the Bible as a tool in their archaeological work. Archaeologists including Steven Ortiz, Titus Kennedy, Amnon Ben-Tor, Aren Maeir, Jeff Chadwick, and Shimon Gibson each affirm that the biblical text is a valuable, sometimes essential, resource for interpreting what they find in the ground.

title: Exploring Joshua's Altar in Israel
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Mount Ebal near ancient Shechem to examine the stone altar excavated by Adam Zertal in the 1980s, identified as the altar Joshua built. He addresses the objection that the altar's location doesn't overlook Shechem, arguing the Bible specifies no exact spot on the mountain and that an eastward orientation — matching the biblical pattern for altars facing sunrise — better explains the site's placement. He connects Mount Ebal's role as the "mountain of curses" (per Deuteronomy's blessing/curse ceremony) and its inscribed copy of the Law to Paul's argument in Galatians that all under the law are under a curse, from which Christ redeemed believers.

title: Excavated Canaanite High Place: "the sin of the Amorites"
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel examines archaeologist Stewart Macalister's 1902 excavation of a Canaanite high place at Gezer, where he found standing stones, an altar, and disturbing evidence of child sacrifice — including burned infant remains in jars and the severed bones of young girls. Using the Bible's descriptions of Amorite worship and its condemnation of child sacrifice to Molech, Macalister and later archaeologists like Kathleen Kenyon interpreted these finds as confirming the Bible's charges of Canaanite iniquity — an interpretation Joel argues later scholarship has downplayed for being "politically incorrect." He closes by connecting this to humanity's shared sinfulness and to Rahab, an Amorite from Jericho who was spared through faith.

title: Unearthing the Prophecy of Jesus' Birthplace
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel examines the fulfillment of Micah's prophecy that a ruler would come from Bethlehem, made roughly 700 years before Jesus's birth and preserved even earlier on a Dead Sea Scroll fragment dated to 125 BC. He traces early extrabiblical testimony from Justin Martyr and Origen describing Jesus's birth in a Bethlehem cave, connects this to Luke's account of no room in the guest quarters, and notes ongoing excavations near the Church of the Nativity confirming a first-century village at the site — presenting this as evidence for both the Bible's historical accuracy and its prophetic authority.

title: Jericho Unearthed: The Archaeology of Jericho Explained
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel brings together archaeologists Peter Parr, Bryant Wood, and Randall Price at Jericho to examine the long-running debate over whether the site's archaeological evidence matches the biblical account of its conquest. He walks through the discovery of a collapsed mud-brick wall, a thick fire-destruction layer with burned grain stores, and evidence the city lay abandoned afterward — all consistent with Joshua's account — before diving into the pottery-dating dispute between John Garstang (c. 1400 BC, matching the Bible) and Kathleen Kenyon (c. 1550 BC), and using 1 Kings' chronology to argue for the biblical date of the conquest.

title: Test of a Prophet: The Bible vs. Joseph Smith
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel applies the Bible's "test of a prophet" from Deuteronomy — that a true prophet's predictions must come true — to both biblical and Mormon prophets. With linguist Christopher Rico, Dead Sea Scrolls expert Randall Price, and archaeologist Gabriel Barkay, he shows how Micah's Bethlehem prophecy, Isaiah's House of David prophecy, David's prophecy of pierced hands and feet, and Daniel's prediction of the Messiah's death before the Temple's destruction were all preserved in pre-Christian manuscripts and fulfilled in Jesus. By contrast, he examines Book of Mormon prophecies (Nephi, Alma) and Joseph Smith's own predictions and alterations to biblical text (including John 1:1 and Romans 4:16) as failing this same test.

title: The Place in Israel Where Archaeology was Born
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel tells the story of Flinders Petrie, considered the father of archaeology, and his 1890 excavation at Tell el-Hesi — the birthplace of pottery chronology. Petrie identified the site as biblical Lachish and used the Bible's account of the city's destructions (by Joshua's conquest, later by Sennacherib of Assyria, and later still by Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon) to date the site's occupation layers. Joel notes that while Petrie later turned out to be mistaken about Tell el-Hesi being Lachish (the actual site was later identified at Tell ed-Duweir), his pioneering, Bible-driven methodology still laid the foundation for modern archaeological dating.

title: Is this where Jesus was tried by Pontius Pilate?
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel and archaeologist Shimon Gibson examine the 1970s excavation of a monumental gate complex on Jerusalem's western hill — part of Herod the Great's palace, later used by Pontius Pilate as his residence and seat of judgment. They connect the excavated stone pavement and judgment platform (bema) to the Gospel of John's account of Jesus's trial at "Gabbatha, the Stone Pavement," and use Luke's detail that Simon of Cyrene was coming in "from the country" to argue this western gate — not the more commonly shown eastern gate, which actually dates to Hadrian's later rebuilding — is the true site of Jesus's trial, flogging, and the start of his walk to the cross.

title: Evidence That King David’s Descendants Survived In Exile
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Babylon and then Berlin to examine what he considers the most significant discovery from Robert Koldewey's excavations: a cache of cuneiform "ration tablets" from Nebuchadnezzar's palace listing oil rations given to "Yakin, king of Judah" — matching the biblical King Jehoiachin, exiled to Babylon. He connects this find to God's covenant promise that David's dynasty would endure forever, showing how 2 Kings distinguishes the captive-but-legitimate king Jehoiachin from his uncle Zedekiah (whose line was destroyed), arguing this tablet is archaeological confirmation that David's line survived the Babylonian exile — a lineage Luke traces forward to Jesus.

title: The Jesus Tomb...UNMASKED!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel investigates the claims of the documentary "The Lost Tomb of Jesus," which argued that the 1980 Talpiot tomb discovery contained the bones of Jesus and his wife. Interviewing the tomb's original excavators (Shimon Gibson, Amos Kloner), an epigrapher, and philosopher William Lane Craig, he shows that the tomb's names were extremely common for the period, the "James ossuary" connection is unsupported, a symbol claimed as an early Christian marker was actually a mason's mark, and the DNA evidence cited to suggest a married couple has been misrepresented — concluding the documentary manipulates evidence and interviews to support a predetermined, non-historical thesis.

title: The OLDEST copy of Scripture ever found! (Even older than the Dead Sea Scrolls)
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel visits Ketef Hinnom in Jerusalem with archaeologist Gabriel Barkay to revisit his 1979 discovery of two tiny silver scrolls in an untouched tomb repository — found only after a young volunteer accidentally broke through a collapsed false floor. Inscribed with the earliest known biblical verses, predating the Dead Sea Scrolls by centuries, the scrolls contain versions of the Priestly Benediction from the Book of Numbers, naming Yahweh, and date to the 7th century BC, the time of the prophet Jeremiah and the First Temple period.

title: Archaeology for "the Star who will come from Jacob"
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels through Jordan tracing the geography behind Balaam's "star prophecy" — visiting the Balaam inscription at the Jordan National Museum, the site of Shittim (Tell el-Hammam), and the three high places (Bamoth-baal, Pisgah/Mount Nebo, and Beth-peor) from which Balaam viewed Israel's camp before prophesying that "a star will come out of Jacob." He argues the star symbolized deity in the ancient world, making this a prophecy that Israel's God would become an Israelite king, and connects it to the Magi's journey in Matthew, who likely traveled the same Roman road past Beth-peor on their way to worship the star's fulfillment: Jesus.

title: Archaeology and the Resurrection of Lazarus
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel visits al-Eizariya (preserving the name "Lazarus"), just east of Jerusalem on the Mount of Olives, to examine the traditional tomb of Lazarus and the site of ancient Bethany, excavated in 1949-1953 by Sylvester Saller. He traces continuous veneration of the tomb back to Eusebius's 4th-century account, connects the excavated village's location to the Gospel's description of Bethany as "less than two miles from Jerusalem," and shows a stack of five successive churches built over the site — arguing the tomb's uninterrupted commemoration and matching biblical geography support its authenticity as the site where Jesus raised Lazarus.

title: Search for the Tower of Babel
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Babylon and the well-preserved ziggurat at Ur to explain what the Tower of Babel would have looked like, then examines Robert Koldewey's excavation of Babylon's ziggurat, Etemenanki, confirming ancient records of its 90-meter base and towering height. He also visits Eridu, a site some scholars propose as an alternative candidate, arguing the biblical text specifically points to Babel/Babylon. He traces the symbolic use of Babylon's tower through Daniel's account of Nebuchadnezzar's pride and Revelation's judgment on "Babylon the great," framing the tower as humanity's failed attempt to reach God apart from Christ.

title: The Bible vs. the Book of Mormon
author: Expedition Bible
description: A documentary comparing the historical, archaeological, and geographic claims of the Bible against those of the Book of Mormon, featuring interviews with archaeologists, anthropologists, linguists, and geographers across multiple countries. It argues the Bible's places, peoples, and material culture are extensively confirmed by archaeology, while the Book of Mormon's claimed civilizations, cities, technologies (metal, coinage, horses), and language leave no corresponding archaeological trace.

title: The Exodus Pharaoh EXPLAINED!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Egypt to identify the pharaoh of the Exodus, using the ancient historian Manetho (preserved through Josephus) to establish the name Amenhotep, then testing this against biblical chronology from 1 Kings' 480-year figure and other clues (the length of the predecessor's reign, whether the successor was a firstborn son) to argue Amenhotep II is the best match. He also addresses the rival "late date" theory built around Ramesses II, arguing it fails on multiple counts and relies on reinterpreting or dismissing key biblical texts like Judges 11:26 and Acts 7.

title: PENIEL: Where Jacob saw the Face of God and lived
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel and his son backpack to Tulul edh-Dhahab in Jordan, identified since 1877 as biblical Peniel, where Jacob wrestled with a divine figure and was renamed Israel. He traces archaeological matches across the site's history — Iron Age I occupation matching the Judges period, and Iron Age II fortification walls matching Jeroboam's building project in 1 Kings — and argues from Hosea that the "man" Jacob wrestled with was God himself.

title: Discovering the MOABITE STONE...MATCHES the Bible!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel tells the dramatic story of the Moabite Stone (Mesha Stele), discovered in 1868 at Dibon by missionary Frederick Klein, then smashed by Bedouin before French scholar Charles Clermont-Ganneau pieced it back together using a paper "squeeze" and recovered fragments. He connects the inscription's boasts by King Mesha of Moab — who names both Omri, king of Israel, and Israel's God Yahweh — to the biblical account in 2 Kings, then visits Ataroth and Nebo, cities Mesha claims to have conquered, showing how the inscription's details (including the tribe of Gad's occupation of the region from Numbers) independently corroborate the biblical record.

title: The Temple Mount--Where it IS. Where it ISN'T. What is it FOR?
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel traces roughly 4,000 years of history on Mount Moriah/the Temple Mount — from Abraham's near-sacrifice of Isaac, to David's altar on Araunah's threshing floor, to Solomon's, Zerubbabel's, and Herod's temples, through Hadrian's pagan shrine and the Dome of the Rock — using 2 Chronicles 3:1 to establish all these events occurred on the same site. He argues archaeological evidence around (though not on) the platform, including a massive rubble pile from the AD 70 destruction, confirms Jesus's prophecy that the temple buildings would be utterly torn down, and closes by connecting the site's substitutionary-sacrifice theme to Jesus's crucifixion and Isaiah 53's suffering servant.

title: Bible Evidence Unearthed at Nineveh!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Mosul, Iraq to explore Nineveh's ruins, tracing Austen Henry Layard's 1849 excavation of Sennacherib's palace, where a stone relief and cuneiform inscription confirmed the site's identity and connected it to Sennacherib, the biblical king of Assyria. He shows how the palace's main showroom depicts the Assyrian siege of Lachish — matching excavated remains of Lachish's siege ramp — and connects Sennacherib's own boastful inscription (naming Hezekiah) to the biblical account of Assyria's invasion of Judah, arguing the Bible's silence and the Assyrian record's silence both confirm Jerusalem alone escaped conquest, as 2 Kings describes. He closes with Nineveh's earlier repentance under Jonah's preaching and its later prophesied destruction, connecting it to Jesus's reference to the "sign of Jonah."

title: Searching for The Garden of Eden's Pishon River
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Saudi Arabia and Iraq to identify the biblical Pishon River, one of four rivers said to flow from Eden. Using Genesis's description of the land of Havila as "opposite Egypt toward Assyria," he argues for a southern Iraq location for Eden rather than the traditional northern Turkey/Armenia proposal, then follows Wadi Rumah — a massive dry ancient riverbed discovered via satellite imagery — across the Arabian Peninsula, matching its geology, gold deposits, and trade-route commodities to the biblical description of Havila's resources.

title: Sodom burned—Zoar did NOT: The full story of the discovery of the Cities of the Plain!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel traces William Foxwell Albright's 1924 expedition to locate the five biblical "cities of the plain," which found the early Bronze Age site of Bab edh-Dhra south of the Dead Sea. He follows subsequent discoveries — Numeira, Fifa, Khanazir, and Safi (identified as Zoar) — showing four sites bear fire-destruction layers while Zoar alone shows continuous occupation into later periods, matching Genesis's account that only Zoar was spared. He argues this southern location fits the biblical geography (Ezekiel, Deuteronomy, Genesis 10 and 19) far better than the rival "Tall el-Hammam as Sodom" theory north of the Dead Sea, and closes by connecting Zoar's survival to salvation through the righteousness of one man — paralleling Christ.

title: How we KNOW the dates for the Old Testament!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel and his son Barry explain how the "Assyrian eponym canon" tablets, discovered in Ashurbanipal's library at Nineveh, allowed 19th-century scholar George Smith to pin an exact BC date to Assyrian chronology using a recorded solar eclipse (June 15, 763 BC), astronomically verifiable using NASA data. He shows how this anchors both Assyrian and biblical chronology through a shared reference point — Sennacherib's invasion of Judah in 2 Kings 18 — allowing the biblical date of the Exodus to be recalculated to 1446 BC. He closes by speculating that this same 763 BC eclipse may have coincided with Jonah's preaching to Nineveh, contrasting the city's repentance with Jerusalem's later rejection of Jesus's similar warning.

title: The Discovery of Joshua's Great Witness Stone at Shechem
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel tells the story of Ernst Sellin's 1926 excavation at Shechem, where a massive carved standing stone and temple were uncovered, and the bitter dispute between Sellin and successor Gabriel Welter over its identification as a sacred Israelite pillar — Welter even smashed it further by hurling it into a pit before it was later recovered and re-erected. He connects the stone and temple ("Beth-berith"/"El-berith") to the events of Judges 8-9 involving Abimelech, and argues, following G. Ernest Wright, that it may be the same "witness stone" Joshua set up during the covenant renewal at Shechem in Joshua 24.

title: Where Jesus Was Crucified: The archaeological evidence!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel tests the authenticity of the traditional Golgotha site beneath Jerusalem's Church of the Holy Sepulchre against the rival "Skull Hill" (Gordon's Calvary) proposal. He cites Virgilio Corbo's 1960s excavation finding a first-century garden layer matching John's account, Nahman Avigad's discovery of a matching city gate and wall showing the site was outside Jerusalem's walls at the time, and Hadrian's deliberate construction of a Venus temple over the site — all pointing to continuous veneration, in contrast to Skull Hill's complete lack of archaeological commemoration before 1842. He also highlights a rare early pilgrim inscription reading "Lord, we will go" discovered near the site in 1975.

title: Tomb of the Exodus Pharaoh: What Was Found & Why You Don't Know About It!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel and his son travel to the Valley of the Kings to explore the 1898 excavation of Amenhotep II's tomb by French archaeologist Victor Loret, retracing Loret's discovery of the pharaoh's mummy — covered in unusual boil-like sores — along with the mummy of his son Webensenu, who died before his father. He connects these finds to the biblical account of the Exodus: the plague of boils, the death of Pharaoh's firstborn son, and Thutmose III's unusually long 54-year reign matching the "long period" Moses spent in Midian, arguing Amenhotep II best fits the biblical criteria for the Exodus Pharaoh.

title: "The Problem" of Joshua's Ai...SOLVED!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel traces the decades-long scholarly dispute over the identification and archaeology of biblical Ai — from John Garstang's 1928 excavation confirming the biblical battle account, through Joseph Callaway's 1960s-70s dig that found no late Bronze Age occupation, to his own 2019 excavation at Khirbet et-Tell. He walks through the topographical details of Joshua 8's battle (Joshua's camp, the ambush hill, a massive stone pile over the city gate) matching the site precisely, and argues Callaway's contradictory findings stemmed from training under Kathleen Kenyon rather than genuine absence of late Bronze Age pottery — evidence his own team's 2019 dig confirmed.

title: #1 Evidence for Israel's Conquest of the Promised Land...other than the Bible!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel travels to Amarna, Egypt, site of the 1887 discovery of the Amarna letters — diplomatic tablets sent by Canaanite city-state rulers to Pharaohs Amenhotep III and Akhenaten. Visiting Jerusalem, Shechem, Lachish, Gezer, and Hazor, he examines letters describing attacks by a group called the "Habiru," arguing (following early scholars like Nutson and Garstang) that the Habiru are the Hebrew Israelites, since the letters' details — a besieged Jerusalem, Shechem's bloodless surrender, Lachish's and Hazor's conquests, and Gezer's successful resistance — closely match the biblical accounts in Joshua and Judges of Israel's conquest of Canaan.

title: EXPEDITION ABRAHAM: From his birthplace to the Promised Land!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel and his team retrace Abraham's roughly 1,000-mile journey from Ur of the Chaldeans, crossing Iraq, Syria, Turkey, Jordan, and Israel over six weeks, following the Euphrates and Balikh rivers to Harran, then the Jabbok River and Wadi Farah route into Canaan used later by Jacob. He connects each geographical stage — Ur's excavated moon-god temple, Harran's Nabonidus inscriptions, the hills of Gilead, and the crossing point at Adam — to the biblical accounts of Abraham's and Jacob's journeys, closing at Shechem, the endpoint of Abraham's journey of faith.

title: Where God Divided the Sea...Exploring the Exodus!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel investigates the traditional site of the Exodus sea crossing at the Gulf of Suez, using Josephus's first-century account and later Christian pilgrim writings (Egeria, Felix Fabri) to locate the crossing at a roughly six-mile-wide point flanked by mountain ranges, matching Exodus's description of Israel being "shut in" by wilderness terrain. After being turned away from the traditional site by an Egyptian military base, he and his team kayak into the Gulf to survey the geography firsthand, arguing the site's difficulty and hopelessness were intentional — God leading Israel into a trap to demonstrate that their deliverance was to be entirely miraculous.

title: Caesarea: The City that Changed the World!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel explores the archaeology of Caesarea, Herod the Great's Roman-style port city built for emperor worship, tracing its transformation into a center of early Christianity. He connects excavated temples to Augustus and Tiberius (including the Pilate Stone) with Peter's vision and preaching to Cornelius in Acts 10, Herod Agrippa I's death as described in both Acts 12 and Josephus, and Paul's imprisonment and trials in Herod's palace and hippodrome recounted in Acts 23-26 — closing with the site's eventual physical transformation, as an octagonal church was built over the ruins of the burned temple to Augustus.

title: This will convince you that God is REAL!
author: Expedition Bible
description: Joel presents five archaeological evidences that God's name, Yahweh, has been continuously known "from generation to generation" as promised in Exodus 3:15 — the 15th-century BC Soleb inscription in Sudan, the 9th-century BC Moabite Stone naming both Israel and Yahweh, the 7th-century BC Ketef Hinnom silver scrolls found in Jerusalem, the Dead Sea Scrolls' repeated use of the divine name, and modern Jewish Bibles still using it today. He contrasts this endurance with the forgotten gods of Israel's ancient rivals (per Sennacherib's taunt in 2 Kings 18-19) and connects Yahweh's name to Jesus, whose Hebrew name Yeshua means "Yahweh saves."
